subject: general
question: The distance between the parts to be joined in a weld is known as ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __Root Gap.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Root gap__ is the distance between the parts to be joined during welding.
 
• It ensures proper fusion and penetration of the weld.
 
• The correct root gap depends on the welding process and material thickness.
 
• A too small or too large root gap can lead to welding defects.
 
• It is a critical parameter in ensuring weld quality and strength.
 
• Proper welding training helps maintain the ideal root gap during fabrication.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Reinforcement:**

 
 
• It refers to the extra weld metal above the surface of the welded joint.
 
• Excessive reinforcement can weaken the weld joint.
 
 
 
• **Fusion Penetration:**
 
 
• It describes the depth to which the weld metal fuses with the base metal.
 
• Proper penetration ensures strong and defect-free joints.
 
 
 
• **Leg Length:**
 
 
• It is the distance from the toe of the weld to the root in a fillet weld.
 
• Leg length is crucial for determining the strength of the weld.
